description: The American Housing Survey is the most complete national housing survey in the United States, run since 1973. It is sponsored by the Department of Housing and Urban Development and conducted by the U.S. Census Bureau. It is a longitudinal survey of housing units, held every two years in odd-numbered years, with samples redrawn in 1985, 2015 and 2025; from the 2025 sample it moves to continuous collection. It measures the size, composition and quality of the housing stock and how it changes as it ages: the physical condition of homes and neighbourhoods, the costs of financing and maintaining them, and the characteristics of the occupants. Coverage is the nation and major metropolitan areas; the data page lists survey years from 1973 to 2023. Access: public use microdata files in SAS and ASCII and summary tables, with tables for 2015 onwards only in the online Table Creator; older annual, national and metropolitan files, back to 1976, are archived as studies at ICPSR. Licence: U.S. federal statistics in the public domain; free. Caveats: a sample survey with sampling error, and design breaks at each new sample. Simulation uses are housing-stock condition and age inputs to exposure and vulnerability models, and housing capacity and recovery planning. Related records: the U.S. national structure inventory and other U.S. building inventories.
